title: Residuals
intro: Calculate and interpret residuals and use residual patterns to assess a linear model.

moments.title: Prediction errors
moments.text: A residual measures observed response minus predicted response.

moments.title: Keep the subtraction order
moments.text: Subtract the model prediction from the actual response.

moments.title: Positive residuals
moments.text: A positive residual means the model underpredicted the observed response.

moments.title: Negative residuals
moments.text: A negative residual means the model overpredicted.

moments.title: Plot residuals
moments.text: Compare residuals with x or with predicted responses.

moments.title: A useful linear model
moments.text: Look for residuals without a systematic pattern around zero.

moments.title: Curvature
moments.text: Systematic curvature suggests the straight-line form misses part of the association.

moments.title: Voltage example
moments.text: Calculate and interpret an error in the response units.

cards.name: Residual
cards.text: $e=y-\hat y$. It is a vertical prediction error in response units.

cards.name: Sign
cards.text: Positive means observed above predicted, so the model underpredicted; negative means overpredicted.

cards.name: Residual plots
cards.text: Plot residuals against x or fitted responses and look for systematic patterns.

cards.name: Model assessment
cards.text: Random-looking scatter around zero supports a linear form. Curvature suggests the form is inappropriate; changing spread also deserves attention.

questions.q: The video uses $\hat y=4.70+2.14x$ for voltage in volts from wind speed x in meters per second. At x=15, observed voltage is 36.9 V. Find the residual.

work.text: The observation is above the model by this amount.

questions.answer: The actual voltage is 0.10 V higher than predicted; the model underpredicts this observation.

questions.obj: Recover an observation from its residual
questions.q: Supplementary example: a delivery-time model predicts 35 minutes for an order. Its residual is −4 minutes. Find the actual delivery time.

work.text: Add the residual to the prediction.
The actual time is lower than the prediction, so the model overpredicts by 4 minutes.

traps.title: Reverse subtraction
traps.weak: A residual is predicted minus actual.

traps.title: Sign reversal
traps.weak: A positive residual means the prediction was too high.
traps.better: A positive residual means the observation was higher than predicted, so the prediction was too low.

traps.title: Units
traps.weak: A residual is measured in x units.
traps.better: It is a difference of response values, so use response units.

traps.title: Curvature ignored
traps.weak: A large correlation makes a curved residual plot acceptable.
traps.better: Curvature suggests the straight-line model is not capturing the association adequately.

questions.stem: Observed response is 52 and predicted response is 47. The residual is:
why: Adding values is not a residual.

opts: The observation is 6 kg above predicted
The prediction is 6 kg above the observation
why: A negative residual puts the observation below predicted.
A residual does not determine the sign of x.

questions.stem: A clear U-shaped residual pattern suggests:
opts: A linear model misses systematic curvature
why: The errors are systematic rather than random around zero.
Residual curvature does not fix a specific correlation.

questions.stem: A fitted value is 20 and the residual is 3. What is the observed response?
why: This subtracts instead of adding the residual.

sections.title: Write a complete response
sections.prompt: A model predicts cooling time in minutes as $\hat y=10+2x$, where x is batch mass in kilograms. A 6-kg batch actually takes 25 minutes to cool. A residual plot for all batches shows an upward curve.
parts: (a) Calculate and interpret this batch's residual.
(b) For another batch the prediction is 30 minutes and the residual is −3. Find and interpret its observed time.
(c) Assess the suitability of the linear model using the residual plot.
sample: (a) The prediction is 10+2(6)=22 minutes. The residual is 25−22=3 minutes: the actual cooling time is 3 minutes longer than predicted, so the model underpredicts.
(b) Observed time is 30+(−3)=27 minutes. The model overpredicts cooling time by 3 minutes.

(c) The upward curve indicates a systematic pattern in the errors, so a straight-line model does not adequately capture the relationship. Investigate a more suitable form rather than relying only on a correlation value.
checklist: Computes the residual with correct subtraction.
Interprets sign and magnitude in minutes.
Uses residual curvature to question linear form.
